questions.stem: Reviewers who had grown used to the {1} of the journal's book pages were startled by the new critic's debut, a {2} dissection of a celebrated biography that left nothing of its central claim standing.
questions.explanation: "Startled" demands that the old pages be the opposite of the new essay: inert, low-energy, going nowhere — torpor. Asperity (harshness) or rigor would make a cutting debut unsurprising rather than startling. In the second blank only trenchant explains an analysis that dismantles the claim; turgid (bloated) and vacuous (empty) describe writing that could not do that.

questions.stem: Because the drafters regarded any reference to "occupied" territory as {1} to a verdict already delivered against them, the delegation bristled with theatrical {2} at a single adjective in the preamble.
questions.explanation: The causal "Because" requires that one word be treated as counting, in effect, as a condemnation — the exact work tantamount does; immaterial would remove any motive for objecting. "Theatrical" and "a single adjective" mark the reaction as over-ready wounded pride, which is umbrage rather than candor or humility.

questions.stem: Malaria kept Ross bedridden for weeks, and long after the fever broke he remained sunk in a {1} so complete that even lifting a pen across the page exhausted him.
questions.explanation: The evidence is bodily — no strength to move a pen — so the blank needs a noun for drained physical inertia, which torpor and lassitude both supply. Ennui is mental boredom, not depleted energy, and abeyance is the suspension of a process rather than a state of a body; vivacity and ferment invert the sense.

questions.stem: Hazlitt's essays on the Lake poets survive less for their generosity than for their {1} analysis, which isolates the precise assumption on which each poet's reputation had been resting.
questions.explanation: "Isolates the precise assumption" praises analysis that cuts straight to the load-bearing point, which is what trenchant and incisive jointly mean. Lucid promises only clarity and mordant only biting tone, neither of which is accuracy of penetration; turgid and bombastic describe inflated prose and contradict the compliment.

questions.stem: For a Roman commander, quitting his province before a successor arrived was {1} to desertion, whatever justifications he later laid before the Senate.
questions.explanation: The act is not formally desertion, yet the concessive clause insists it was judged as though it were — precisely the gap tantamount names. The other options all take "to" but assert relations (irrelevance, sequence, vulnerability) that leave the sentence's verdict unmade.

questions.stem: Johnson, who could absorb a savage review without flinching, nonetheless took {1} at the bookseller's suggestion that his dictionary be abridged for schoolboys.
questions.explanation: Only umbrage completes the fixed idiom "take ___ at," and only umbrage carries the raised eyebrow the contrast invites: a man indifferent to real attacks bridling at a small slight to his dignity. Ire, rancor, indignation and chagrin name related feelings but are not taken at anything.

questions.stem: Leaving the flood-control fund unspent for a third straight year was, the editorial argued, {1} to an admission that the state had no policy whatever — {2} dressed up as fiscal caution.
questions.explanation: The editorial is stripping away a technicality to say what inaction really amounts to, so the first blank must be tantamount; incidental and antecedent describe side-relations or sequence, not equivalence in effect. "Dressed up as" requires something discreditable underneath, and torpor — inertia rather than deliberate thrift — is the only option that squares with having no policy at all.

questions.stem: Members long accustomed to the committee's emollient minutes received the auditor's report with {1}, since its {2} summary of the pension shortfall named, in three sentences, the decision each of them had hoped would go unmentioned.
questions.explanation: Men whose evasions have been exposed react with wounded, defensive offence — umbrage — not with eagerness or thanks. The second blank must praise a summary that is both brief and unanswerable: trenchant, whereas prolix would contradict "three sentences" and anodyne would contradict the naming of what was to stay hidden.
